summary: Iran's Navy launched four anti-ship cruise missiles toward the Strait of Hormuz from Sirik while CENTCOM enforced a blockade redirecting 105 commercial vessels in the Arabian Sea. Saudi Arabia faces escalating pressure after a drone attack shut down its East-West pipeline, cutting all crude oil supplies to European refiners, and the US approved a $24.3 billion F-35 sale to Riyadh. The IDF reinforced all sectors ahead of Yom Kippur as security incidents continued in the West Bank and Lebanon.

Saudi Arabia will supply no crude oil to European refiners next month after a drone attack shut down its East-West pipeline. (Source: @Faytuks_Network/7213)

sections.executive_summary: Iran's Navy launched four anti-ship cruise missiles from Sirik toward the Strait of Hormuz while CENTCOM enforced a US blockade redirecting 105 commercial vessels in the Arabian Sea. Saudi Arabia faces dual crises: a drone attack on its East-West pipeline cutting all European crude supplies, and an intensifying Yemen war with 112,000 displaced. The IDF reinforced all commands ahead of Yom Kippur as the US approved a $24.3 billion F-35 sale to Riyadh.

points: Iranian Navy launched four anti-ship cruise missiles from the Sirik area in southern Iran toward the Strait of Hormuz, a direct demonstration of naval power in the critical shipping chokepoint amid escalating US blockade enforcement. (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/392929)

CENTCOM reported that its forces have redirected 105 commercial vessels as of September 18 to enforce the US blockade against Iran, with USS Boxer and its embarked Marine Expeditionary Unit continuing enforcement operations in the Arabian Sea. (Source: @shin_persian/10172)

An Iranian military exercise dubbed 'Janfadayans' (Sacrifice for Iran) was held in Tehran with participation of 313,000 elements, described by the Associated Press as the largest show of force since the war began. Thousands also thronged Tehran streets for a 'Sacrifice for Iran' rally. (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/392924, @presstv/207337)

Russia and China vetoed a US-backed resolution against Iran at the UN Security Council, with 15 nations including Iran, China, and Russia stressing that peaceful nuclear facilities under IAEA Safeguards must not be targeted or threatened with attack. (Source: @presstv/207326, @presstv/207340)

Saudi Arabia has contacted Iran to request mediation with Yemen, according to Abdullah al-Naami, a senior Ansarallah political bureau member, who stated Yemen will not agree to any ceasefire until Saudi Arabia lifts its blockade. Oman is currently mediating between Saudi Arabia and Yemen. (Source: @SharghDaily/184439)

The IDF Chief of Staff ordered reinforcement of forces across Northern, Southern, and Central Commands ahead of Yom Kippur, with dedicated reinforcement companies in each sector, a senior commander present in each command, increased armed aircraft, and additional missile ships at sea. Reserve companies will be available for allocation to different commands alongside defined General Staff alert units. (Source: @inon_yttach/10039)

Shin Bet and Israel Police arrested Hamdan Hamdan, a 32-year-old Israeli citizen from Majd al-Kurum, on suspicion of security offenses involving contact with a foreign agent. Investigation revealed he maintained contact for several months with a foreign female agent from Lebanon who directed him to perform security tasks, with payment attempts made through purchases of products in Israel by the foreign entity. An indictment will be filed on September 20, 2026. (Source: @New_security8200/203835)

A shooting report was received regarding gunfire and identification of a hit on an Israeli civilian's vehicle near the village of Al-Mu'ayyir in the Binyamin region, with no casualties. Security forces launched scans and imposed roadblocks on the village area, and an investigation was opened. (Source: @idf_telegram/25155, @New_security8200/203841)

Sufian Abu Zaida, a senior Palestinian Authority politician close to Mohammad Dahlan, revealed himself as the source who passed a warning to Shin Bet in mid-September that Yahya Sinwar was planning a major attack on Israel. He stated he will share details about contacts he managed between Israel and Hamas before October 7 aimed at reaching a deal to release Israeli hostages in exchange for hundreds of Palestinian prisoners. (Source: @yediotnews25/135107)

A Maariv poll shows Likud at a low of 18 seats, with Gadi Eisenkot leading Benjamin Netanyahu on the question of suitability for prime minister, with 48% support versus 40%. (Source: @yediotnews25/135105)

A shooting incident targeted an Israeli civilian vehicle near the village of Al-Mu'ayyir in the Binyamin region of the West Bank, with no casualties reported. Security forces conducted scans, imposed roadblocks on the village area, and opened an investigation to collect findings and evidence. (Source: @idf_telegram/25155)

Sufian Abu Zaida revealed he was the source who passed a warning to Shin Bet in mid-September that Yahya Sinwar was planning a large-scale attack on Israel, and that he had been managing contacts between Israel and Hamas before October 7 aimed at a hostage-for-prisoners deal. (Source: @yediotnews25/135107)

October 8 newspaper headlines reported hundreds murdered and dozens kidnapped, while Abu Shahada spoke about extracting political fruits from Hamas's campaign, highlighting the disconnect between the scale of the attack and internal Palestinian political framing. (Source: @amitsegal/65003)
A loud explosion heard in Beirut's southern suburb (Dahieh) was caused by a sound bomb dropped in the Bourj al-Barajneh area, according to Lebanese reports. (Source: @redlinkleb/43639)
Artillery shelling was reported targeting Zuta al-Sharqiya (Zoutr al-Sharqiya) in southern Lebanon, with live mapping of the incident. (Source: @redlinkleb/43646)
Warplanes were reported operating in southern Lebanon, with live tracking of the aircraft. (Source: @redlinkleb/43652)

A feature marking two years after Israeli pager attacks in Lebanon recounted the experiences of victims Basil, Bayan, and Haidar, who described devastating injuries, profound loss, and their determination to rebuild their lives without abandoning their commitments. (Source: @presstv/207336)

Shin Bet investigation revealed that an arrested Israeli citizen from Majd al-Kurum was directed by a foreign female agent from Lebanon to perform security tasks, with payment attempted through product purchases in Israel transferred to the suspect. (Source: @New_security8200/203835)

Protests and road blockades occurred in front of a private generator in Kirkuk province, Iraq, due to the owner's refusal to operate it, reflecting ongoing civil unrest over basic services. (Source: @naya_foriraq/90889)

French President Emmanuel Macron announced that Paris will cooperate with Iraq and Jordan to build an oil and gas pipeline from Iraq to the European market, while also calling for a diplomatic solution to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and accelerating gas storage projects in Europe to reduce energy price pressure. (Source: @SharghDaily/184442)

Saudi Arabia will supply no crude oil to European refiners next month after a drone attack forced the shutdown of its key East-West pipeline, with the supply cut applying to all European customers with long-term contracts, Bloomberg reported. (Source: @Faytuks_Network/7213)

The US State Department approved a potential $24.3 billion sale of F-35 fighter jets to Saudi Arabia as Riyadh intensifies its military aggression against Yemen, significantly upgrading Saudi air capability. (Source: @presstv/207334)

Saudi civil defense reported the danger was cleared in Khamis Mushait, while Saudi sirens were placed on high alert with messages referencing escalation and blockade tactics. An emergency warning was also issued for Jeddah. (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/392952, @rasedal3ado138e/392951, @shin_persian/10177)

Saudi aviation continued targeting civilian sites in Taiz, Yemen, while a Yemeni government source reported mass desertion of Saudi coalition mercenaries in Jabal Habashi in Taiz city. (Source: @naya_foriraq/90888, @naya_foriraq/90927)

At least 112,000 people have been displaced from their homes in Yemen in the last two weeks due to Houthi advances, with nearly 3,000 people fleeing by sea to Djibouti, according to the UN migration agency. (Source: @asafroz/53545)

Pro-government Giants forces destroyed four additional Houthi vehicles on the Kahboub front near the Bab al-Mandab Strait, while residents of the newly liberated city of Al-Mokha rallied in support of Yemen's Armed Forces. (Source: @shin_persian/10175, @presstv/207327)

South Korea's president stated Seoul will not send forces or military equipment that could lead to participation in war, but may take minimum necessary measures to protect commercial shipping, crude oil transport, and citizen security in the Strait of Hormuz region. (Source: @VahidOnline/78433)

sections.threat_assessment: The simultaneous launch of Iranian anti-ship cruise missiles toward the Strait of Hormuz and CENTCOM's blockade enforcement with 105 redirected vessels create a high-risk flashpoint for direct naval confrontation. Saudi Arabia's pipeline shutdown and total European crude supply cutoff represent a major escalation in the Yemen war's spillover, while the approved $24.3 billion F-35 sale to Riyadh signals imminent Saudi air capability upgrades. The IDF's multi-command Yom Kippur reinforcement and the arrest of an Israeli citizen recruited by a Lebanese agent indicate persistent multi-front threats facing Israel.
sections.regional_response: Saudi Arabia's request for Iranian mediation via Oman marks a significant diplomatic shift, though Ansarallah's refusal of any ceasefire without lifting the Yemen blockade limits near-term de-escalation prospects. France's announcement of an Iraq-to-Europe oil and gas pipeline with Jordanian cooperation reflects European efforts to diversify energy routes away from Hormuz-dependent supply. South Korea's conditional willingness to protect shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, while refusing combat participation, illustrates the growing international pressure to secure maritime corridors. Russia and China's veto of the US-backed anti-Iran resolution at the UN Security Council underscores deepening great-power polarization over the conflict.
sections.intelligence_notes: Sufian Abu Zaida's self-identification as the source of the pre-October 7 Sinwar attack warning to Shin Bet may generate significant political fallout regarding intelligence handling and Israel-Hamas backchannel negotiations. The Iranian 'Janfadayans' exercise with 313,000 participants in Tehran represents an unprecedented mobilization display that may signal regime confidence or internal consolidation pressures. The Lebanese agent's recruitment of an Israeli citizen from Majd al-Kurum demonstrates continued hostile intelligence operations from Lebanon targeting Israeli Arab communities during wartime. Saudi sirens on high alert and emergency warnings in Jeddah suggest ongoing active threats to Saudi civilian infrastructure from Yemeni forces.
